description: Replication of the Talent vs Luck (TvL) agent-based model: A. Pluchino, A. E. Biondo, A. Rapisarda, Advances in Complex Systems 21(3-4) 1850014 (2018), arXiv:1802.07068. One world = N careers of 40 years; capital is 'success' in dimensionless units, not money.
source_parameters: Section 2 and 2.1 of the paper: N=1000, talent ~ Normal(0.6, 0.1) truncated to [0,1], C(0)=10, 80 steps of six months, NE=500 event-points, 50% lucky, world 201x201 patches with periodic borders, events move 2 patches per step in a random direction, an event hits an agent inside a circle of radius 1 patch; lucky hit doubles capital with probability equal to talent, unlucky hit halves it.
hit_rule_note: The paper does not say what happens when several event-points hit one agent in the same six months. 'each': every hitting event acts (lucky ones each give a chance to double, unlucky ones each halve). 'once': at most one lucky and one unlucky action per step. Chosen by comparing both with the paper's published results (see episodes/talent-luck/DESIGN.md).
method: Each run is one world of the Talent vs Luck model (1000 careers, 40 years). Exact histograms over all worlds; capital = C0 * 2**k. Best performer = agent(s) with the highest capital in a world; ties share weight equally.
